text:
Noah (support): FYI a few PRO customers reporting large p99 latencies and occasional 504s for /v1/generate since ~03:10 UTC. Most traffic served from hosted A100 pool.

Elena (eng-runtime): Any recent infra/driver changes?

Ravi (eng-infra): We shipped a driver & kernel combo earlier in the maintenance window at 02:50 (NVIDIA driver 555.xx + kernel 6.6.0-rc2) to the pilot cluster. It was supposed to be canary only.

Noah (support): tickets show a spike aligned to that window. Sample app trace: 
```
2025-11-11T03:12:05Z id=req-9876 route=gpt-large queue_ms=300 runtime_ms=7200 host_block_ms=6900 gpu_wait_ms=0 result=504
2025-11-11T03:12:05Z runtime: loading shard 9 from /dev/nvme0n1p1 io_ms=6800
```

Tess (eng-sre): host_block_ms >> gpu_wait_ms usually points at host IO. Could be NVMe firmware reset or kernel IO path regression. Ravi, can you pull nvme smart and dmesg?

Ravi (eng-infra): collecting now from 6 suspect nodes. Preliminary nvme-cli: repeated vendor reset events and controller fatal errors at 03:10-03:13. SMART shows increased media errors for SN range.

nvme-watch: alert: nvme_reset_count high on node-77,node-79,node-82.

Elena (eng-runtime): runtime logs show many cold-starts hitting disk; our prefetch tried to load kv shards concurrently which amplifies IO. If the disk hiccups, the runtime blocks waiting for read().

Noah (support): customers want ETA and mitigation.

Tess (eng-sre): quick plan:
- Isolate affected nodes from serving pool (set node state=drain)
- Redirect new traffic off pilot pool to stable pool
- Roll back driver/firmware on most-affected hosts or boot from previous image
- Add temporary runtime throttle: serialize shard reads per process to reduce parallel IO storm

Ravi (eng-infra): starting drain on node-77,79,82. Initiating rollback on node-79. Boot image rollback might be faster than in-place firmware patch.

deploy-bot: rollout rollback initiated by Ravi for nodes [node-79] — job id 20251111-rbk-11

Elena (eng-runtime): I can push a quick hotfix to reduce concurrent prefetches: change PREFETCH_PARALLEL=2 (was 8) and add a host_block_ms circuit breaker to fallback to quantized model variant. I'll open a PR and patch canary config.

Noah (support): drafting customer note: "We identified host storage interruptions after a maintenance update to a subset of hosts. We're draining affected machines, rolling back the update, and applying runtime mitigations to reduce cold-start IO. Expect significant improvement within 30-60 minutes."

Tess (eng-sre): + add "no data loss, only availability" and provide escalation contact.

Ravi (eng-infra): node-79 rollback completed at 03:32; nvme resets stopped. iostat: 
```
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1         45.0    12.0   2048   128.0   5.3  0.05   0.6   0.4  1.2   0.01  8.2
```

Elena (eng-runtime): fleet p95/p99 dropping on rolled back nodes. Aggregated latency still slightly elevated due to remaining nodes draining and some queued requests.

Ravi (eng-infra): vendor confirmed firmware regression in build X.Y.Z when combined with kernel 6.6.0-rc2 in certain controller batches. They recommend rollback and will provide patched firmware next week. Support ticket opened (NV-20251111).

Tess (eng-sre): action items:
- Ravi: coordinate vendor RCA and schedule full rollback for pilot pool off-hours
- Elena: merge runtime prefetch throttle + host_block_ms circuit breaker
- Ops: add NVMe health probe to node agent to auto-drain on reset spikes
- Support: send final customer update when all nodes rolled back

Noah (support): will update customers. One requested SLA credit guidance; routing to finance ops.

Elena (eng-runtime): repro notes for postmortem:
1) boot node with kernel 6.6.0-rc2 + firmware X.Y.Z on NVMe
2) run runtime with small memory limit so model pages from disk
3) flood cold-start requests (200-400 concurrent) to force parallel shard reads
4) capture dmesg, nvme-cli logs, iostat, and runtime traces - expect nvme controller resets and host_block_ms spikes

Tess (eng-sre): collection commands: 
```
sudo apt-get install nvme-cli sysstat
sudo nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1 > /tmp/smart.log
iostat -x 1 30 > /tmp/iostat.log
sudo dmesg -T | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg.log
sudo cat /proc/interrupts > /tmp/interrupts.log
```

nvme-watch: vendor response: known regression, patch ETA 7 days.

Ravi (eng-infra): scheduling fleet rollback window. Will also add a deploy guard to block kernel+fw rollouts unless canary success rate >= 90% for 2 hours.

Noah (support): customers acknowledged mitigation note; incidents reduced. Marking this thread mitigated; will follow up in postmortem doc. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
